status: Evidence-ranked hypotheses, not an isolated causal result

setup.judge: GPT-6 Luna medium, averaged reversed anonymous orders

observed_normalization_example.implication: A small score difference can yield a large standardized negative advantage. Whether this particular deduction was justified remains a human rubric question.

interpretation_hypotheses.hypothesis: Grading variation plus group standardization creates unreliable relative-learning signals.
interpretation_hypotheses.evidence: 45/448 candidate scores disagree across swapped calls; one identical proof receives 2 versus 7; near-ceiling normalization example above.
interpretation_hypotheses.limit: Both orders are averaged for actual training. Disagreement is not a measured error rate, and presentation order is confounded with stochastic variation.

interpretation_hypotheses.hypothesis: One-question gradients and few clean repetitions make improvement noisy and cross-question interference plausible.
interpretation_hypotheses.evidence: One problem and 32 answers per step, versus 64 problems and 2048 answers in the supplied Ian recipe. Only one or two updates per question under the repaired judge.
interpretation_hypotheses.limit: No larger-prompt-batch or longer-training control was run.

interpretation_hypotheses.hypothesis: Long, repetitive answers and terminal-reward credit assignment waste compute and dilute useful proof feedback.
interpretation_hypotheses.evidence: Matched mean output length 52355 to 56344 tokens; cap fraction 0.17634 to 0.22991. The same sequence-level advantage is broadcast across the response and loss is averaged over its active tokens.
interpretation_hypotheses.limit: No matched shorter-budget or concise-output control was run. Several short mathematical arguments are correct, while a sampled zero makes false claims.

interpretation_hypotheses.hypothesis: Truncated sampling and support replay may restrict useful exploration and direct token gradients.
interpretation_hypotheses.evidence: 54.514% of latest-run token positions have singleton support. Their conditional log probability is zero and its direct score-function gradient is zero.
interpretation_hypotheses.limit: Predictable syntax can also have singleton support. Other positions still update shared parameters. This percentage alone does not establish a bug or cause.

health_checks.limits: Finite metrics and per-token ESS do not prove gradient correctness for mathematical truth, full-trajectory alignment, or an optimal learning rate.

overall_result.interpretation: No clear reward gain; the evidence does not isolate a single cause.
